solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, number freed: 5 across to 6); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Record of financial transactions on a yearly basis for each advert

parts.note: PA is short for per annum, Latin for each year
per means for each, as in ten pounds per head
a trail is a trailer advertising a coming programme or film

explanation.surface: An accountant's ledger records, year by year, what was spent on each advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on a yearly basis' looks like part of the definition but supplies PA (per annum).
explanation.definitionFit: A documentary trail of receipts and statements lets auditors follow where money went.

clue.text: Pop Idol in Greece once covering Westlife's Number One

indicators.note: covering means the god's name wraps round the next letter

parts.note: Pan was a god worshipped in ancient Greece

indicators.note: the number one of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pop talent show contestant in Greece covering a Westlife chart-topper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' is British slang for pledging an item at a pawnbroker's ('pop goes the weasel'), not music. Westlife is an Irish boy band.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop something is informal for pledging it to a pawnbroker in return for a loan.

clue.text: Change old nappy where daughter's left brilliant array

indicators.note: change signals the remaining letters are rearranged
left means departed, so the daughter's letter is removed

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent changes an old nappy now the daughter has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from OLDNAPPY to get OLNAPPY, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A panoply is an impressive, splendid display or full collection of things.

clue.text: Nosily watching masseuse behaving amorously

parts.note: a masseuse rubs clients, so is a rubber
necking is kissing and cuddling

explanation.surface: A masseuse caught getting amorous with a client.
explanation.definitionFit: Craning the neck to gawp at an accident or scene is nosy gawking.

clue.text: Get back, say, bad weather coating

indicators.note: coating means the word for bad weather surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: rain is bad weather
eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'a fruit, say'

explanation.surface: A complaint that bad weather has coated everything.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover or retrieve something lost is to get it back.

clue.text: Lazy member of ruling party to observe fast?

parts.note: a party in power is said to be in
to do something such as a ritual is to observe it
Lent is the Christian period of fasting

explanation.surface: Is a politician lazy if they choose to keep a religious fast?
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' is not speed but the Lenten fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means habitually idle and averse to effort.

clue.text: Sell business

definitions.meaning: to betray or inform on someone, as in selling a friend down the river
a trading outlet or firm, as in setting up a small concern

explanation.surface: A short instruction to dispose of a company.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is slang for betraying someone to the police; the other is a retail premises or workshop.

clue.text: More than one carrion feeder has to be fed with any end of lettuce when desperate

indicators.note: fed with means the word has takes the other letters inside it
desperate suggests wild disorder, so these letters are scrambled
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A starving creature reduced to eating any scrap of lettuce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when desperate' scrambles the word any with the final letter of lettuce, and 'to be fed with' places that after the first letter of has.
explanation.definitionFit: These African scavengers feed mostly on carcasses; the plural matches 'more than one'.

clue.text: Heads of state allowing church to usurp scientific system, giving historical justifications

indicators.note: usurp means to take another's place, so the church letters replace the scientific ones

parts.note: presidents head republics
SI is the International System of units used in science
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Political leaders letting the church overturn science, citing past examples.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier cases used to justify a later decision are authorities from history.

clue.text: One rabbiting's turn to kill

parts.note: to wind is to turn, as with a handle or a clock key
to bag is to kill game when hunting

explanation.surface: A rabbit's turn comes round to be shot by the hunter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbiting' is British slang for talking on and on (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' = talk), not hunting rabbits.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiresome talker who never stops chattering is someone rabbiting on, British slang for prattling.

clue.text: Go off fruit that's mostly bad inside

indicators.note: inside signals the shortened word for bad sits within the fruit

parts.note: the date is the fruit of the date palm

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter of the word for bad is kept

parts.note: evil means bad or wicked

explanation.surface: A warning that a piece of fruit is rotten within and will spoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go off' reads as fruit spoiling, but it means to stray. 'mostly' drops the last letter of the word for bad; 'inside' places the rest within the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to stray or depart from a set course, which is going off route.

clue.text: Depraved band from which there's no escape

definitions.note: the definition describes the noun as a trap one cannot leave

parts.note: vicious once meant depraved or immoral
a circle is a ring or band

explanation.surface: A wicked gang that nobody ever gets out of.
explanation.definitionFit: A cycle of cause and effect where each problem worsens the other is an inescapable loop.

clue.text: Excuse for rule-breaking that might be endorsed by grammar police?

definitions.text: Excuse for rule-breaking that might be endorsed by grammar police?

parts.words: Excuse for rule-breaking that might be endorsed by grammar police?
parts.note: a writer's freedom to bend rules of language is pictured as a driving permit that pedants, like traffic police, could stamp with penalty points

explanation.surface: Pedants who police language might approve an excuse for breaking its rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endorsed' here is the British sense of police marking penalty points on a driving licence, not approving.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers claim freedom to ignore grammar or fact for artistic effect; the second word is a permit, which traffic police endorse.

clue.text: Surfer's position should be this open

definitions.meaning: a surfer stands on top of the surfboard
honest and legitimate, with nothing hidden

explanation.surface: Advice that a surfer should stand clearly in view.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means legitimate and transparent; literally, a surfer stands atop the board.

clue.text: Remix done by unknown

definitions.note: used as a noun, the unknown, the realm past life or knowledge

indicators.note: a remix rearranges an existing track, so the words that follow are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A DJ's remix credited to an anonymous producer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unknown' looks like the algebraic Y, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The great hereafter, what lies past human knowledge, is called the unknown.

clue.text: Finish with or go out with one given money?

parts.note: an end is a finish
to see someone is to date them

explanation.surface: A choice between ending a relationship and dating someone with cash to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The person a cheque is signed over to receives payment, so is one handed money.

clue.text: Male social worker taking note is unmoved

indicators.note: taking means the pair of words take in the extra letter

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
the ant is a social insect and a worker

explanation.surface: A male social worker who takes notes stays unemotional.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a caseworker but an ant, an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water does not flow, so it is still and motionless.

clue.text: Appetite lacking in second half, Rovers after comeback beginning to attack rivals?

indicators.note: a comeback turns things round, so that half-word is read backwards
only the opening half of the team name Rovers is kept
the beginning of attack is its first letter

parts.note: City is a common football club name, a rival side to a Rovers team

explanation.surface: A football report: a team losing appetite after half-time, then a Rovers comeback attacking their rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking in second half' keeps the first three letters of Rovers and 'after comeback' turns them round; 'beginning to' takes the first letter of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Voracity is a greedy, ravenous hunger, a fierce eagerness to eat.

clue.text: Start to restrain English player, one liable to have a meltdown if things go disastrously?

definitions.text: one liable to have a meltdown if things go disastrously?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: An English actor who storms off when a performance goes badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meltdown' suggests a tantrum but is a nuclear core melting.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear power plant core can overheat and melt down when safety systems fail.

clue.text: Guard conquistador taking French art to the far west

indicators.note: taking signals the French word is lifted out of the conquistador's name
the far west of an across entry is its left-hand end, where the lifted letters go

parts.note: Hernan Cortes was the Spanish conquistador who conquered the Aztecs
es is French for 'art' as in 'thou art' (tu es)

explanation.surface: A conquistador's bodyguard is seen carrying French paintings off to the Wild West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French art' is the verb, 'tu es' (you are), not painting: CORTES with its final ES taken to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is someone who accompanies and protects, a guard.

clue.text: Noise during exam resulting in third?

indicators.note: during means the noise happens within the exam

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
din is a loud noise

explanation.surface: A disturbance in the exam hall leads to a third-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'third' looks like a degree result, but is an example of a number showing position, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Third is an example of a number indicating position in a sequence.

clue.text: Content I censor's held to act like clickbait

indicators.note: held means the letters are contained within the words before it

explanation.surface: A web censor deems some content to be clickbait.
explanation.definitionFit: Clickbait lures readers with tempting headlines, which is what alluring or tempting means.

clue.text: Remembering to enter carrying alcohol? Genius!

parts.note: to bear is to carry
to go in is to enter
gin is an alcoholic spirit
a mind is a brilliant thinker, as in one of the great minds

explanation.surface: Someone congratulates themselves on remembering to bring drink when arriving at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to enter' piece sits inside the 'carrying alcohol' pair, as if carried by them, before the genius word.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in your thoughts, not forgetting it, is remembering.

clue.text: Bank lacking power to respond

definitions.note: the definition is a verb, as in 'bank on'

indicators.note: lacking means the letter for power is missing

parts.note: to reply is to respond

explanation.surface: A bank with no electricity cannot answer customers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is not a building but the verb in 'bank on', to depend.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on someone is to count on or depend on them.

clue.text: Caribbean island opposed to bird droppings withdrawing objection

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: withdrawing signals the word of objection is taken out of the droppings

parts.note: guano is the accumulated excrement of seabirds, used as fertiliser
no is a word of objection or refusal

explanation.surface: An island's residents oppose bird mess, then drop their objection.
explanation.definitionFit: Antigua is the main island of Antigua and Barbuda in the eastern Caribbean.

clue.text: Smoking material used by ecclesiastical swingers?

definitions.text: Smoking material used by ecclesiastical swingers?

parts.words: Smoking material used by ecclesiastical swingers?
parts.note: church servers swing a censer of aromatic resin during services, so the swingers are thurifers, not partygoers

explanation.surface: Racy hint at clergy who swing and the substances they smoke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swingers' suggests partner swapping, but the swinging is of a thurible on its chain in church.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragrant resin burned for its scented smoke, especially in religious ceremonies.

clue.text: Blow repair

definitions.meaning: a mild exclamation of annoyance, like blast or drat
to mend a hole in fabric by weaving thread across it

explanation.surface: A puncture or a blowout that needs mending.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a mild curse, a polite substitute for damn; the other is mending socks with needle and wool.

clue.text: Leader in Economist, article truly in heavenly style

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its first letter

parts.note: the is the definite article
really means truly

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial written in a lofty, otherworldly tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a newspaper editorial, but it means the first letter of Economist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means celestial or delicately light, so the adverb describes acting in a heavenly manner.
